# 4 Ezra Chapter 9 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — Fourth vision

---

**1** He answered: Keep careful track of time in your mind. When you see that a portion of the signs I described has already occurred,

**2** then you will understand: this is the exact moment when the Most High is about to move against the world he made.

**3** When you see in the world: upheavals among peoples, tumults among nations, plots among kings, bewilderment among leaders, terror among rulers —

**4** then know that the Most High was speaking of exactly these things from before your time, from the very beginning.

**5** For everything that happens in this world has a beginning and an end, and the same is true of all that the Most High has decreed: the openings are marked by wonders and mighty deeds; the endings are marked by payback and by signs.

**6** And anyone who has been saved and manages to escape through their works and by the faith you have embraced —

**7** that person will be kept safe from the dangers I described and will witness my salvation within my land and within my borders. For I have set those lands apart for myself from the beginning.

**8** Those who have misused my ways will then be stunned. Those who threw them aside in contempt will live in torment.

**9** Because those who in their lifetime received good things and never gave thanks for them; those who had my law available and chose to disregard it, who had the chance to repent and threw that away too —

**10** they will have to learn all of this through suffering after death.

**11** So don't waste your energy wondering how the wicked will be punished. Ask instead how the righteous will be saved — because it is for their sake the world was made and the ages began.

**12** I said: I have said it before, I say it now, and I will go on saying it: there are more who perish than those who are saved —

**13** the way a wave is bigger than a drop.

**14** He answered: The field matches the seed. The flowers match their colors. The work matches what it is worth. The farmer matches the threshing floor.

**15** For there was a time — before the world existed for them to live in — when I was already preparing for those who now live. No one opposed me then because no one yet existed.

**16** Now these same people, created in a world that provides unlimited food and inexhaustible pasture, have ruined themselves through their own choices.

**17** I looked at my world and found it wrecked. I looked at my earth and found it in danger because of what the people living in it had been doing.

**18** I looked, and barely managed to spare it. I saved myself one person out of many — one out of a countless mass.

**19** And the descendants of that one are who rules over you now, saying to themselves: We alone have gotten what no one else ever got.

**20** And now I feel no joy over the multitude who have already perished — because those alive today have started doing the same evil things right in front of me as those of the first world did.

**21** I said: But you gave Adam to the earth — he was your own creation. And you didn't force his descendants to sin; you allowed it to him through his own free desire. Yet it wasn't a crowd of righteous people who stood before you then — just one man counted among the righteous.

**22** And I said: I know, O LORD, that the Most High is called compassionate — because he shows compassion to those not yet born; and merciful — because he shows mercy to those who come back to his law;

**23** and patient — because he bears with those who have sinned as his own creatures;

**24** and generous — because he prefers to give rather than to take;

**25** and deeply compassionate — because he keeps multiplying his compassion, for those living today and for those of generations past and for those of the age still to come.

**26** For if he did not keep multiplying his mercy, the world and everything made in it could not survive.

**27** He gives — because he is a giver. He heals — because he is a healer. He plants — because he is a planter. He cuts off — because he cuts off. He dries up — because he dries up. He makes flow — because he makes things flow. He creates — because he creates. He destroys — because he destroys.

**28** He guides — because he guides. He lifts up — because he lifts up.

**29** No one can undo what he has made. No one can overturn what he has approved.

**30** There is no one else beside him. So he governs his creation by his own wisdom and by nothing outside of it.

**31** I said: So what am I supposed to do? I have reached the point where I can't easily praise you for these things, and I can't easily say nothing about them either.

**32** The people coming into the world in the last times have no roadmap — but they do have things set out before them in the present that they are supposed to follow.

**33** About those things I will not be silent — I will speak about them. But about other matters I will not speak without being told to.

**34** He said: As I told you before, and now say again: go and eat the flowers of the field. No meat, no wine — only the flowers.

**35** And keep praying to the Most High without stopping. I will come and speak with you.

**36** I went, as he told me, to the field called Ardat. I sat among the flowers and ate the herbs of the field, and the food satisfied me.

**37** Seven days later I was lying in the grass when the anguish returned to my heart as before.

**38** I opened my mouth and began to speak before the Most High.

**39** And then I saw a woman coming toward me. She was in mourning, wailing loudly, deeply heartbroken. Her clothes were torn and ashes were heaped on her head.

**40** I let go of what I had been thinking and turned to face her.

**41** I asked: Why are you crying? What is breaking your heart?

**42** She said: Please, my lord, leave me alone and let me grieve. I have sorrows to add to sorrows. My heart is in agony and I am utterly humiliated.

**43** I said: Tell me what happened. And she said: I was barren. I had no child for thirty years, though I had a husband all that time.

**44** Every day and night for all those thirty years, hour after hour, I petitioned the Most High.

**45** After thirty years God heard me, your servant, and noticed my desperate condition, and took pity on my distress, and gave me a son. I was overjoyed — I and my husband and all the neighbors. We gave enormous praise to the Mighty One.

**46** I raised him with so much effort and love. When he grew up and the time came, I found him a wife and prepared a wedding feast.

**47** But when my son went into his wedding chamber, he collapsed and died.
